Wash hands.
Stand to the right of the patient. Ask the patient to expose the entire abdomen, draping the pelvic area and lower extremities.
Verbalize inspection of abdomen for color, contour, symmetry, and movement.
Auscultate abdomen (prior to palpation or percussion) in all four quadrants (right upper, right lower, left upper, left lower).
Palpate abdomen LIGHTLY in all four quadrants (right upper, right lower, left upper, left lower).
Palpate abdomen DEEPLY in all quadrants (right upper, right lower, left upper, left lower).
Check for rebound tenderness: deep palpation with quick release of hand in four quadrants. Ask if patient feels pain with palpation or release of hand.
Percuss abdomen in all four quadrants (right upper, right lower, left upper, left lower).

Palpate liver edge: place left hand on back between right rib cage and hip; place right hand in right upper quadrant pressing inward and upward. Ask the patient to take a deep breath as the edge is palpated.

Percuss liver span: begin percussing in the right lower quadrant and proceed proximally until the transition from tympanic to dull identified. Then, begin in the right mid-clavicular line over the lung and proceed over the anterior chest until the transition between resonance and dull is identified.
Palpate spleen: place left hand on back behind left rib cage and lift; place right hand in left upper quadrant pressing inward and upward while asking the patient to take a deep breath.
Palpate aorta in the upper abdomen slightly to the left of the midline.

Ask the patient to sit up and percuss costovertebral angles bilaterally using fist percussion over your hand with palm placed on the costovertebral angle to assess for kidney tenderness. Ask if patient feels pain.

You did not greet me, greeted me disrespectfully, OR were unclear about your role in the team
You greeted me respectfully, used your full name, and clearly explained your role in the healthcare team.
Your greeting was respectful, confident, and thorough. From the beginning, I felt comfortable to share my concerns.
You did not ask about or spent little time on my concerns, missed significant details about my concerns, OR framed questions in a way that did not allow me to tell my story.

You asked about my concern and allowed me adequate time to share my story. You got the essential information. There may have been some missed opportunities to gain a deeper understanding of my concern.
You allowed me to fully share my story in a conversational and comfortable way. You got all of the essential information and all or almost all of the details surrounding my concerns.
You never asked about my perspective of my concerns or illness, never asked about my expectations for treatment, OR did not understand how these concerns impact me emotionally or functionally.
You made effort to understand my perspective of my concerns, my expectations for treatment, and how these concerns impact me emotionally or functionally.
You thoroughly explored and demonstrated understanding of my perspective on my concerns including my expectations for treatment and how these concerns impact me emotionally and functionally.
You did not encourage me to ask questions. You rarely provided me with information about my concern. You did not help me to understand my symptoms or possible diagnosis.
You answered questions but did not check for my understanding. You provided me with an appropriate amount and complexity of information.
You clearly answered my questions. You provided me with clear information about my concern at a level that was easy for me to understand. You checked to be sure I understood.
You frequently used medical jargon or frequently made several frightening or alarming comments. You addressed sensitive topics in an abrupt manner, or a manner which expressed judgment.
You occasionally used medical jargon without explaining it in layman’s terms. You rarely made unduly frightening comments. You addressed sensitive topics professionally but in a detached manner.

You used medical terms as needed, and explained them in a way I could understand without my asking. You explained serious concerns and findings in a clear but compassionate way. You addressed sensitive topics in a way that made me to feel at ease.
You did not share information on different treatment options. You did not include me in decision-making. You did not assess my willingness to execute the plan.
You presented me with information about different treatment options, but did not assess my preference for treatment planning.
You presented me with different treatment options, provided rationale for each, and assessed my treatment preference. You helped me choose an option in collaborative way.
You did not maintain eye contact or your eye contact was uncomfortable. Your body language was closed or off-putting. You rarely reflected my emotions. I did not feel connected with as a person.

You maintained eye contact. Your body language was open. You reflected my emotions a few times in the encounter. You were pleasant but distant. I did not feel that genuine interest in me as a person was demonstrated.
Your body language and demeanor was warm and inviting. You frequently reflected my emotions. We connected well, and I felt genuine interest in me as a person was demonstrated.
You left the encounter abruptly. You did not summarize the encounter. You did not provide me with instructions on what to do next, or what to do if I had questions.
You summarized the facts of my concern but not my perspective. You provided me with information on what would happen next, but did not open the door for additional contact if I had questions.
You summarized the facts of my concern and my perspective. You provided me with instructions on what to do next including what to do if I had questions.
You were difficult to talk with, I felt uncomfortable, or the encounter was disorganized or confusing.
You were pleasant to talk with for the encounter, and I rarely felt uncomfortable. Your organization was variable, but I generally understood your line of questioning.

You were easy to talk with. I felt comfortable and respected throughout the encounter. Your organization was excellent such that I felt that we were understanding one another and collaborating throughout the encounter.
